pages.text: With More Than 15 Million Made, This Iconic Car Became the World’s Most Popular on This Day in 1972 Skip to main content The Beetle became the most produced—and most popular—car ever made, dethroning industry legend Henry Ford and his Model T. Photo by George Argeroplos/Newsday RM via Getty Images Volkswagen Beetle No. 15,007,034 rolled off the assembly line on February 17, 1972, in a feat that made automotive history. The Beetle became the most produced—and most popular—car ever made, dethroning industry legend Henry Ford and his Model T. The Beetle began driving on this path to success in 1933 when Nazi leader Adolf Hitler ordered Ferdinand Porsche, the founder of the eponymous luxury car brand, to create “Volkswagen,” which roughly translates from German to English as “the people’s car.” Porsche was instructed to create a small, affordable vehicle that could transport two adults and three children. This simple mandate yielded a distinctive, curved shape. The initial intent of this shape was to be aerodynamic and efficient. However, it quickly caught attention, turning into an icon of the German auto world even as it spread Nazi ideals of the “Volk,” Hitler’s word for ethnic Germans, and popularized one of Hitler’s signature public works programs, the autobahn system. Initially called the “ Kraft durch Freude ” (“Strength Through Joy”) or “KdF” car, the vehicle was a rolling advertisement for Hitler’s campaign of the same name, which provided leisure activities for German workers financed by compulsory donations. The review will run from 4 to 14 October, with teams working at the national level and across all eight divisions. Initiated at the request of the Government, the review will comprehensively assess the performance of immunization and vaccine-preventable disease surveillance across Bangladesh, identifying strengths, gaps and priority actions to ensure every person is reached with life-saving vaccines. Bangladesh’s EPI has delivered major public health gains since its establishment in 1979. The country has remained polio-free for more than 15 years, sustained elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus, achieved control of rubella, and introduced new vaccines to protect children and communities. They have also been excluded from conflict prevention and resolution efforts. Despite increased awareness and mobilization at the local and international levels, women and girls in conflict continue to face multiple challenges. A lack of high-level leadership committed to integrating women’s rights, including in Security Council negotiations and in peace talks, means women are often left out. Grassroots organizations working on women’s local-level peacebuilding and service provision struggle to get adequate and consistent funding. That was the question at the top of Brittany’s mind after seeing Alesha Harris’ Is God Is , a film following twin sisters on a quest to kill their abusive father. The film has been a surprise hit, but there’s a subsection of men who felt this portrayal of a ‘bad’ Black man was in poor taste. That made Brittany wonder: in the pantheon of vengeance films featuring female protagonists, what does it mean to seek justice? And what does catharsis look like when the villain is sometimes patriarchy itself? pages.description: The Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) includes protections for individuals who elect breast reconstruction in connection with a mastectomy. pages.text: Women's Nations League: Republic of Ireland draw Spain as NI take on Poland - BBC Sport Image source, Press Eye/Getty Images Image caption, The 2027 Nations League will take place from February to June By Andy Gray BBC Sport NI Journalist Published 3 November 2026 The Republic of Ireland will face world champions Spain in the 2027 Nations League, while Northern Ireland take on Poland in League B. Poland, who face the Republic of Ireland in a Women's World Cup play-off in December, join Northern Ireland, Finland and Belarus in League B3. Carla Ward's Republic of Ireland side have been tasked with a difficult group in League A against Nations League holders Spain, Norway and Switzerland. Fixtures have yet to be confirmed by Uefa, but the Nations League will be played across the international windows in February/March, April and June. The Republic of Ireland have been handed one of the most difficult draws available as they look to retain their place in League A. Spain, who won the 2024 and 2025 editions of the Nations League, are the headline team but Norway and Switzerland are also difficult opponents. With key players such as Caroline Graham Hansen and Ada Hegerbeg, Norway are ranked 13th in the world and while the Republic of Ireland, in 21st, are ranked higher than Switzerland, they will be tough opposition. Northern Ireland have never been relegated or promoted from League B since the competition was launched in 2023, and their aim will to have another solid campaign. pages.text: Women's Nations League: Who are Republic of Ireland's Nations League opponents? - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Republic of Ireland will face world champions Spain, Norway and Switzerland between February and June next year By Lauren McCann BBC Sport NI Journalist Published 3 November 2026 Republic of Ireland face an uphill battle to qualify for the Olympic Games for the first time after they were drawn against Spain, Norway and Switzerland in the third edition of the Nations League. Carla Ward's side remained in League A following their brilliant performances in Women's World Cup qualifying, but have been handed a tough draw as they look to keep their place in the top tier. The four group winners of League A will progress to the Nations League semi-finals and earn a place at the 2028 Games in LA. Third place will face a promotion/relegation play-off against a League B side, while fourth place will be relegated to the second tier. With all that in mind, BBC Sport NI looks at the Irish's three opponents in greater detail. Net run-rate is the common method for differentiating teams level on points in a limited-overs cricket tournament. It is a formula that measures a team's average margin of victory, or defeat - a side with several big wins will have a positive net run-rate, while those who have suffered sizeable losses will have a negative one. To understand net run-rate, you have to first get your head around run-rate. That is the average number of runs scored per over by a team in the innings of one match - so, for example, a score of 140 off 20 overs for Team A equals seven runs per over. pages.text: Work Opportunity Tax Credit | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Work Opportunity Tax Credit More in This Section Close How to File a WOTC Certification Request Resources Performance Contact Regional Offices What is WOTC? The Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) is a federal tax credit available to employers who invest in American job seekers who have consistently faced barriers to employment. Employers may meet their business needs and claim a tax credit if they hire an individual who is in a WOTC targeted group . Employers must apply for and receive a certification verifying the new hire is a member of a targeted group before they can claim the tax credit. After the required certification is secured, taxable employers claim the WOTC as a general business credit against their income taxes, and tax-exempt employers claim the WOTC against their payroll taxes. WOTC is authorized until December 31, 2025 (Section 113 of Division EE of P.L. 116-260 -- Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021). pages.text: Workers Under 18 | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Workers Under 18 More in This Section Close Foreign Labor I-9 Central Veterans Workers Under 18 The U.S. Department of Labor's Wage and Hour Division (WHD) administers and enforces the federal child labor laws. Generally speaking, the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) sets the minimum age for employment (14 years for non-agricultural jobs), restricts the hours youth under the age of 16 may work, and prohibits youth under the age of 18 from being employed in hazardous occupations. In addition, the FLSA establishes subminimum wage standards for certain employees who are less than 20 years of age, full-time students, student learners, apprentices, and workers with disabilities. Employers generally must have authorization from WHD in order to pay subminimum wage rates. The FLSA's child labor provisions are designed to protect the educational opportunities of youth and prohibit their employment in jobs that are detrimental to their health and safety. The Department's YouthRules! initiative helps promote positive and safe work experiences for young workers. All states also have standards concerning youth employment. When federal and state standards are different, the rules that provide the most protection to young workers will apply. Note that federal employment laws on safety and health, discrimination, benefits, etc. apply to youth, as well as to older workers.

View on TensorFlow.org Run in Google Colab View on GitHub Download notebook When working with tensors that contain a lot of zero values, it is important to store them in a space- and time-efficient manner. Sparse tensors enable efficient storage and processing of tensors that contain a lot of zero values. Sparse tensors are used extensively in encoding schemes like TF-IDF as part of data pre-processing in NLP applications and for pre-processing images with a lot of dark pixels in computer vision applications. Sparse tensors in TensorFlow TensorFlow represents sparse tensors through the tf.sparse.SparseTensor object. Currently, sparse tensors in TensorFlow are encoded using the coordinate list (COO) format. This encoding format is optimized for hyper-sparse matrices such as embeddings. The COO encoding for sparse tensors is comprised of: values : A 1D tensor with shape [N] containing all nonzero values. indices : A 2D tensor with shape [N, rank] , containing the indices of the nonzero values. dense_shape : A 1D tensor with shape [rank] , specifying the shape of the tensor. Occupational Safety and Health Administration OSHA administers the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act . Safety and health conditions in most private industries are regulated by OSHA or OSHA-approved state plans . Nearly every employee in the nation comes under OSHA's jurisdiction with some exceptions such as miners, some transportation workers, many public employees, and the self-employed. Employers subject to the OSH Act also have a general duty to provide work and a workplace free from recognized, serious hazards. OSHA also administers the Whistleblower Protection program, ensuring an employer cannot retaliate by taking "adverse action" against workers who report injuries, safety concerns, or other protected activity. Mine Safety and Health Administration MSHA has responsibility for administration and enforcement of the Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977, which protects the safety and health of workers employed in the nation's mines. pages.description: Early action on diabetes is vital in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Learn how countries are strengthening diabetes prevention, early diagnosis and access to affordable, quality treatment and care through primary health care and SEAHEARTS.
pages.text: World Diabetes Day Skip to main content World Diabetes Day Early action on diabetes 14 November 2026 Statement Reading time: Dr Nilesh Buddha, Officer-in-Charge, WHO South-East Asia Diabetes is one of the fastest growing public health challenges in the WHO South-East Asia Region. An estimated 254 million adults in the Region live with diabetes, with millions undiagnosed, and nearly two-thirds not receiving glucose-lowering treatment. When diagnosed late or managed poorly, diabetes can lead to life-threatening damage to the heart, kidneys, nerves, and eyes. This year, the theme of World Diabetes Day, “Early action on diabetes,” highlights the importance of earlier diagnosis, access to comprehensive care, and reducing stigma to improve the lives of people with diabetes. Early action starts in communities where healthy choices are within reach and symptoms are recognised early. Primary health care is the foundation for early action, enabling early identification of those at risk and prompt diagnosis. Every diagnosis must be followed by affordable, uninterrupted care, in societies that support people living with diabetes rather than stigmatising them. The Region is advancing this agenda through SEAHEARTS, the regional initiative to accelerate cardiovascular disease prevention and control. Member States have committed to placing 70 million people with diabetes on protocol-based management by 2030, and to achieving good glycaemic control in 50% of them. Authoritarian Advances Threaten Rules-Based Order Philippe Bolopion Executive Director Download the easy-to-read version of the World Report The global human rights system is in peril. Under relentless pressure from US President Donald Trump, and persistently undermined by China and Russia, the rules-based international order is being crushed, threatening to take with it the architecture human rights defenders have come to rely on to advance norms and protect freedoms. To defy this trend, governments that still value human rights, alongside social movements, civil society, and international institutions, need to form a strategic alliance to push back. To be fair, the downward spiral predated Trump’s reelection. The democratic wave that began over 50 years ago has given way to what scholars term a “democratic recession.” Democracy is now back to 1985 levels according to some metrics, with 72 percent of the world’s population now living under autocracy. Russia and China are less free today than 20 years ago. And so is the United States. Of course, democracy is not a panacea for human rights violations; the US and other longtime democracies have their own histories of colonial crimes, racism, abusive justice systems, and wartime atrocities. Now a study shows that these intense downpours have become shorter in duration and fewer in number, compressing the same amount of rain into quicker and more extreme events, with implications for flood and drought risk. Chiyuan Miao and colleagues from Beijing Normal University in China analysed daily measurements between 1980 and 2022 from more than 19,000 rain gauges around the world. They found that an average of about half of the world’s rainfall fell during about nine multi-day storms, delivered over a cumulative time of about 28 days.
